_doc: Operational policy facts that the BIS central-bank policy-rate series does not show, disclosed on real-time-era pages for reading the policy rows (never model inputs). Each item is shown only in editions whose last eligible day is on or after its date, the publication date of its cited source. Türkiye 2017: the BIS series is the CBRT one-week repo rate, kept at 8% all year, while the CBRT restricted funding at that rate and supplied the market at the late liquidity window lending rate. Each source fetched and checked (tcmb.gov.tr press releases and MPC decisions). The CBRT's later statement that one-week repo auctions were suspended from 12 Jan 2017 is in Inflation Report 2017-I, whose retrievable PDF was created on 1 Mar 2017; it is not cited because its publication date before the affected cutoffs cannot be shown. Türkiye 2018-2019: the 2017 late-liquidity-window items carry 'until' 2018-05-31 (the last day that arrangement applied) and are not shown after it; the CBRT's simplification of 28 May 2018 (one-week repo rate the funding rate again from 1 Jun 2018) and the 2019 one-week repo auction suspensions (22 Mar, 9 May) and resumptions (8 Apr, reported by ING on 18 Apr; 21 May, Reuters) are each shown from their source's own date. The resumption of 8 Apr 2019 is documented by no fetched source dated before 18 Apr, so the 2019-04-14 edition shows the suspension only. The CBRT press releases and the ING and Arab News pages were fetched and their quoted text checked.

TR.text: the CBRT lowered banks' borrowing limits at its Interbank Money Market to TL 22 billion from 11 Jan 2017 (announced 10 Jan) and to TL 11 billion from 16 Jan 2017, said funding through Borsa Istanbul repo markets 'may be limited' on days deemed necessary, and that banks could meet their remaining liquidity needs 'without limits at late liquidity window funding rate at the end of the day'; the one-week repo rate (the BIS series) stays at 8%, so it understates the CBRT's marginal funding cost from then on
TR.label: CBRT press release, 13 Jan 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the marginal funding (overnight lending) rate from 8.5% to 9.25% and the late liquidity window lending rate from 10% to 11%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 24 Jan 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11% to 11.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 16 Mar 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11.75% to 12.25%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 26 Apr 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 12.25% to 12.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 14 Dec 2017

TR.text: the CBRT completed the simplification of its operational framework, effective 1 Jun 2018: 'One-week repo rate will be the policy rate of the Central Bank. This rate will be equal to the current funding rate (16.50%)', with the overnight borrowing and lending rates 150 basis points below/above it; the one-week repo rate (the BIS series, 8% until then) is again the CBRT's funding rate, so its move from 8% to 16.5% on 1 Jun 2018 aligns the series with the funding cost already in force (the late liquidity window lending rate had been raised to 16.5% on 23 May 2018)
TR.label: CBRT press release, 28 May 2018

TR.text: 'Considering the developments in financial markets, it has been decided to suspend the one-week repo auctions for a period of time' (no end date given); without one-week repo funding, banks' marginal CBRT funding is the overnight lending rate (25.5%, the top of the corridor), above the 24% one-week repo rate that the BIS series shows
TR.label: CBRT press release, 22 Mar 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'started one-week repo auctions again on 8 April, readjusting the effective cost of funding to 24%'
TR.label: ING Think, 'Turkish Central Bank to stay on hold', 18 Apr 2019

TR.text: the CBRT again decided 'to suspend the one-week repo auctions for a period of time'; bankers expected the average cost of funding to rise gradually to 25.5%, against the 24% one-week repo rate
TR.label: CBRT press release, 9 May 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'held a repo auction for the first time in nearly two weeks, reversing a policy tightening step', injecting 17 billion lira, and lowered the lira interest rate in swap transactions to 24% from 25.5%; funding returns to the 24% one-week repo rate
TR.label: Reuters via Arab News, 'Turkish lira weakens after cenbank repos resume, FX purchase move', 21 May 2019
